found: A call holder is most likely to exercise early when all three conditions are met: The call is deep in the money ... The remaining time value is less than the dividend amount ... Expiration is relatively near ... Time value must be less than the dividend for early exercise to make economic sense. ... The writer of that call faces elevated assignment risk the day before the ex-date
suggested_fix: Early exercise of an in-the-money American call just before the ex-dividend date only makes economic sense when the call's remaining extrinsic value (in practice, the same-strike put's extrinsic value) is below the dividend, so a short deep-ITM call in that state faces elevated assignment risk the day before ex-dividend.
